trust_decision.summary: Whether attacker-supplied XML (documents to sign, XDC containers, eForm XSLT/XSD, ASiC manifests) may make the parser resolve external entities/DTDs; decided once in the shared DocumentBuilder factory helper, which only disables external general entities (parameter entities and external DTD loading stay on).

landing_point.why: The advisory names XMLUtils.java; getSecureDocumentBuilder is the only DOM factory in the repo and sets only one XXE feature.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP POST /sign and /batch on the local Autogram server (AutogramServer.java:48,52) -> SigningJob/XDCValidator/visualization -> EFormUtils.getXmlFromDocument (EFormUtils.java:284)
same routes; second hunk site inferred from candidate metadata c_fix_sites=2, possibly Transformer/Schema factory hardening

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No real out-of-scope site: every DOM parse in the repo goes through XMLUtils.getSecureDocumentBuilder, so a single helper change closes all routes; nothing to dismiss.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: eForm XSLTs that declare internal DTD entities (<!DOCTYPE xsl:stylesheet [<!ENTITY ...>]>) are legitimate input; a disallow-doctype-decl fix rejects them, while disabling only external/parameter entities and external DTD loading keeps them working. Its test is currently commented out.

O6_input_shapes: external general entity in document body (already blocked at XMLUtils.java:18)
external parameter entity / external DTD subset (presumed fixed; diff not visible)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: manifest parse using its own DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance() instead of the shared helper
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The ASiC manifest is container metadata that a maintainer could treat as trusted and parse with a quick local factory; it is a WHERE-type sibling only, so it counts as an extra.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: forms.xml/meta.xml parsed via XPath InputSource evaluation (XPathFactory default parser) instead of getXmlFromDocument
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: XPathFactory is already used here and xpath.evaluate(expr, InputSource) is a common shortcut; it is a remote-fetched resource, so it is plausibly argued as trusted.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Set disallow-doctype-decl=true in getSecureDocumentBuilder, which also rejects legitimate XSLTs with internal entity declarations.

out_of_scope_notes: XPath expression built by string concatenation of xdcIdentifier/fsFormId (src/main/java/digital/slovensko/autogram/core/eforms/FsEFormResources.java:58,82); different weakness, not pursued.
unverified: The fix diff file contains only the merge-commit header (fix.diff:1-2) and no hunks, so the exact published change is unknown; fix_sites are inferred from the advisory naming XMLUtils.java and from candidate metadata (c_fix_sites=2, c_site_files=1, single hunk).

O1 counts only the two HTTP routes evidenced at src/main/java/digital/slovensko/autogram/server/AutogramServer.java:48,52; the GUI file-open and CLI signing modes probably reach the same parser too, but this was not traced.

Whether Schema.newValidator() at src/main/java/digital/slovensko/autogram/core/eforms/xdc/XDCValidator.java:83 inherits ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD from the factory; its input is re-serialized by transformElementToString, so a DOCTYPE likely cannot reach it.
DSS library parsing (XMLCanonicalizer at src/main/java/digital/slovensko/autogram/core/eforms/EFormUtils.java:112, SignedDocumentValidator) is outside this repository and was not checked.
single_site red flag assumes the published change is confined to XMLUtils factory helpers, as the metadata indicates.
